recipes.title: Sattu drink
recipes.summary: Filling roasted gram flour drink. No cooking.
steps: Put the sattu in a glass or bottle.
Add a little water and stir into a smooth paste.
Add the rest of the water, salt, lemon and cumin, and stir or shake well.
Drink straight away.
substitutions: Use jaggery instead of salt for a sweet version.
Add chopped onion or green chilli if you have them.
safety: Use only treated or packaged water for soaking, rinsing and mixing.

recipes.title: No-cook lemon poha
recipes.summary: Softened flattened rice with peanuts and lemon.
steps: Rinse the poha briefly in clean water and drain well.
Leave it for 5 minutes to soften.
Mix in salt, sugar and lemon juice.
Top with peanuts and onion or cucumber.
substitutions: Roasted chana or sev instead of peanuts.
Curd instead of lemon, if it is fresh.
safety: Use only treated or packaged water for soaking, rinsing and mixing.
Eat within 2 hours, or within 1 hour in hot weather, unless you can refrigerate it.

recipes.title: Puffed rice bhel
recipes.summary: Crunchy puffed rice with peanuts and chana.
steps: Mix the puffed rice, peanuts and chana.
Add onion and tomato if using.
Season with lemon, salt and chaat masala and eat at once, before it softens.
substitutions: Any dry namkeen or sev can replace part of the puffed rice.
safety: Wash fresh vegetables in treated water before chopping.

recipes.title: Canned chickpea chaat
steps: Check the can is not bulging, leaking or badly dented.
Drain the chickpeas and rinse them in clean water.
Mix with onion, tomato, lemon, salt and chaat masala.
substitutions: Canned rajma or mixed beans.
Roasted chana if you have no cans.
safety: Discard any can that is bulging, leaking, rusted or spurts when opened.
Eat within 2 hours, or within 1 hour in hot weather, unless you can refrigerate it.

recipes.title: Gur, chana and peanuts
recipes.summary: Portable energy snack that keeps for weeks.
steps: Mix everything in a dry, airtight container.
Eat a handful as needed.
substitutions: Add dried fruit, makhana or seeds if available.
safety: Keep the container dry and sealed to stop it going soft or attracting insects.

recipes.title: Bread or khakhra with peanut butter
recipes.summary: Quick, portable meal from shelf staples.
steps: Spread peanut butter on the bread or khakhra.
Add sliced banana if you have one.
substitutions: Jam, honey or chutney instead of peanut butter.
safety: Check bread for mould before eating; throw away the whole loaf if any is mouldy.

recipes.title: Soaked oats
recipes.summary: Oats softened in milk or water. No heat needed.

ingredients.item: UHT or packaged milk, or clean water

steps: Mix the oats with milk or water.
Leave for 15 to 20 minutes until soft.
Sweeten and add nuts or fruit.
substitutions: Poha can be used instead of oats, with a shorter soak.
safety: Use sealed UHT milk, or eat at once if made with fresh milk and there is no refrigerator.
Eat within 2 hours, or within 1 hour in hot weather, unless you can refrigerate it.

recipes.title: One-pot moong dal khichdi
recipes.summary: Soft rice and lentils in one pot. Easy to digest.
equipment: Pot with lid or pressure cooker
steps: Wash the rice and dal together and soak for 20 minutes. Soaking saves fuel.
Drain, then add 3 cups of water, salt and turmeric.
Pressure cook for 3 whistles, or simmer covered for 20 to 25 minutes until soft.
Stir in ghee if using.
substitutions: Masoor dal instead of moong.
Add any vegetables you have.
safety: Serve hot. Cool leftovers quickly and eat them the same day, reheated until steaming.

recipes.title: Quick masoor dal
recipes.summary: Red lentils that cook fast with no soaking.
steps: Rinse the dal.
Boil with water, salt and turmeric, then simmer covered for 15 to 18 minutes until soft.
For tadka, heat oil with cumin and pour over, if fuel allows.
substitutions: Yellow moong dal also cooks quickly.
safety: Keep the lid on to save fuel and water.

recipes.title: Fuel-saving rice
recipes.summary: Rice cooked without draining, so no water is wasted.
steps: Rinse the rice and soak it for 20 minutes, then drain.
Bring the rice and 2 cups of water to the boil.
Cover tightly, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 10 minutes.
Turn off the heat and leave covered for 10 more minutes.
substitutions: Add whole spices or a little ghee for flavour.
safety: Cooked rice left at room temperature can cause food poisoning. Eat it hot and do not keep it for later without refrigeration.

recipes.title: Tawa roti
recipes.summary: Simple flatbread from atta and water.
steps: Mix flour and salt, then add water slowly and knead into a soft dough.
Rest the dough for 10 minutes.
Divide into balls and roll each thin.
Cook on a hot tawa about a minute per side until brown spots appear.
substitutions: Mix in besan or millet flour if atta is short.
Pat by hand if you have no rolling pin.
safety: Wash hands before kneading.

recipes.title: Besan chilla
steps: Whisk besan, water, salt and spices into a smooth batter.
Add onion if using.
Spread a ladle of batter on a hot, lightly oiled tawa.
Cook 2 minutes per side until set and golden.
substitutions: Mix in atta or rice flour if besan is short.
safety: Use only treated or packaged water for soaking, rinsing and mixing.

recipes.title: Rava upma
steps: Dry roast the rava for 2 to 3 minutes and set aside.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds and onion, and cook for a minute.
Add water and salt and bring to the boil.
Stir in the rava slowly, cover and cook on low for 2 to 3 minutes.
substitutions: Poha or broken wheat (dalia), adjusting water and time.
safety: Serve hot.

recipes.title: Egg bhurji
steps: Heat oil and cook the onion for a minute.
Add beaten eggs, salt and chilli.
Stir until fully cooked with no runny parts.
substitutions: Paneer instead of eggs for a vegetarian version.
safety: Cook eggs until firm.
Wash hands and anything that touched raw egg.

recipes.title: Canned rajma
recipes.summary: Kidney-bean curry from a can in 10 minutes.

ingredients.item: tomato, chopped, or 2 tbsp tomato puree

steps: Check the can is not bulging, leaking or badly dented.
Cook onion in oil, then tomato, for a few minutes.
Add the beans with their liquid and salt and spices.
Simmer for 5 minutes until hot through.
substitutions: Canned chickpeas or mixed beans.
safety: Discard any can that is bulging, leaking, rusted or spurts when opened.

recipes.title: Packet noodles with vegetables

ingredients.item: chopped vegetables or a beaten egg (optional)

steps: Boil the water.
Add the vegetables and cook for 1 minute.
Add noodles and seasoning and cook as the packet says.
substitutions: Add leftover dal or chana for protein.
safety: Adding egg makes it non-vegetarian; cook until set.

recipes.title: Retained-heat dal and rice
recipes.summary: Bring to the boil, then let an insulated box finish the cooking to save fuel.
equipment: Insulated box, basket or bedding to wrap the pot
steps: Soak the rice and dal for 20 minutes, then drain.
Add water, salt and turmeric and bring to a full boil.
Boil hard for 5 minutes with the lid on.
Move the closed pot quickly into an insulated box, or wrap it thickly in blankets.
Leave closed for 1 to 2 hours, then check it is soft and still steaming hot.
substitutions: Works for other grains and pulses that cook by simmering.
safety: Food must still be steaming hot when you open it. If it is only warm, bring it back to the boil before eating.
Do not leave food in the box overnight.
Not suitable for meat in emergencies.

sections.title: Do
items: Keep dry food in airtight containers off the floor, in a cool, dry place.
Store food away from fuel, pesticides and cleaning products.
Use older stock first and check dates regularly.

sections.title: During power cuts
items: Keep fridge and freezer doors closed as much as possible.
Perishable food left warm for more than 2 hours should be thrown away.

sections.title: Throw away
items: Cans that are bulging, leaking, badly dented, rusted or spurt when opened.
Food with mould, slime, a sour or unusual smell, or an odd colour.
Food that has touched flood water, unless it is in an undamaged sealed can that you clean first.
Cooked food left at room temperature for more than 2 hours, or 1 hour in hot weather.

sections.title: Rule
items: When in doubt, throw it out. Tasting is not a safe test.

references.title: Food Safety in a Power Outage and Flood
references.publisher: US Department of Agriculture, Food Safety and Inspection Service

references.title: Five Keys to Safer Food Manual

sections.title: Five keys
items: Keep clean: wash hands with soap before handling food and after using the toilet.
Separate raw and cooked food.
Cook thoroughly, especially meat, eggs and seafood.
Keep food at safe temperatures: eat hot food hot and do not leave cooked food out.
Use safe water and fresh, undamaged ingredients.

references.title: Five Keys to Safer Food Manual

sections.title: Do
items: Use separate boards and knives for raw meat or eggs and for ready-to-eat food, or wash them well in between.
Wash hands after handling raw meat, eggs or unwashed vegetables.
Cover food to keep flies and pests off.

sections.title: Do not
items: Put cooked food back on a plate that held raw food.

references.title: Five Keys to Safer Food Manual

safety.title: Drinking-water safety
safety.summary: Safe water for drinking and cooking.

sections.title: Steps
items: Use sealed bottled water or water you have treated.
Boil water at a rolling boil for 1 minute, or use purification tablets as the packet says.
Store treated water covered and pour it out rather than dipping in.

sections.title: More
items: See Survival Handbook › Filtration versus disinfection for full details.
